project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer: Develop and demonstrate wave and tidal energy technology that withstands harsh conditions with low cost and environmental impact.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer: Develop and demonstrate wave and tidal systems and their components. Cover breakthrough work, validation and demonstration, with the core team organising onward funding for third-party breakthrough and validation work.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer: Ocean-energy developers need equipment and connections that withstand marine conditions and cost less to install, operate and maintain.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer: Provide at least three distinct demonstrations and document project progress against annual milestones. Design the third-party grant calls, evaluation, risk plan and deployment decisions.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: Improve cost, reliability, efficiency and sustainability throughout an ocean-energy farm’s life. Coordinate research and validation so promising solutions can move towards use.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer: Share results that can be disclosed and contribute to the Clean Energy Transition Partnership’s knowledge and impact networks (channels for sharing evidence from funded projects). Link the demonstrations to prospects for industrial uptake.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer: The proposal needs at least three independent funded partners in three different eligible countries. At least one must be established in a European Union Member State. The other two must be established in different Member States or countries associated with Horizon Europe (countries formally participating in the European research programme).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer: The consortium needs ocean-energy demonstration skills and a record of managing large projects or awarding third-party grants. Set up an advisory board with independent public and private experts and the relevant European initiatives.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer: The core consortium runs the demonstrations itself and manages all onward grants (funding passed to outside organisations). It can share breakthrough and validation work with third parties. Demonstrations should use at most EUR 24 million of the European grant and project management should stay within 7%.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer: The group appoints a funded partner to lead the work on wave and tidal energy systems and represent it to the funder.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer: TenneT could coordinate the project if it can develop or validate the electrical connection for an ocean-energy demonstrator run by the core consortium. The applicants choose their coordinator (the funded partner that represents the group to the funder).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer: TenneT could take part in wave and tidal energy systems without receiving a grant. As an associated partner (an organisation that works without a grant), it could develop or validate the electrical connection for an ocean-energy demonstrator run by the core consortium. It would cover its own costs and would not count towards the minimum number of funded partners. The source’s national eligibility rules for awards to third parties are separate from the main project’s grant.

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer: TenneT can receive up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow) for qualifying work. The Dutch entity could develop or validate the electrical connection for an ocean-energy demonstrator run by the core consortium. Budget at least 30% of those costs from other resources.
cards.sources:

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer: TenneT could assess power-connection interfaces and monitoring requirements for ocean energy. The project would need a defined engineering or validation role for the Dutch operator.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: The breakthrough strand develops new solutions. The validation strand can test technology developed within the project or by earlier European or national projects.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: The call covers converters, materials, moorings, power connections, condition monitoring, manufacturing and deployment methods.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Cover breakthrough development, validation and demonstration. The core consortium alone runs the demonstrations and must plan at least three with distinct technical focuses.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The work should reach TRL 6–7 (technology readiness level: technology demonstrated in relevant or operational conditions) by project end. The call allows work to start at any maturity level.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Specific conditions

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: Use controlled, monitored and reproducible conditions. Suitable settings include tanks, test rigs, sheltered basins or instrumented real-sea sites.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer: Connect third-party breakthrough and validation grants with the core demonstrations. A later round can validate promising early work without starting the research chain again.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer: Use the International Energy Agency’s Ocean Energy Systems performance measures. Report progress annually and show permits, engineering readiness and a business and implementation plan before each deployment decision.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer: The independent advisory board should include public and private ocean-energy experts. Third-party grants can fund applications that demonstrate value for end users.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer: Before each deployment decision, the demonstrator needs permits and a detailed engineering design that meets applicable standards. Cover relevant safety and environmental risks in the project’s mitigation plan.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Scope

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission indicates EUR 43 million for wave and tidal energy systems. It expects 1 award.
- Grant request: Around EUR 43 million per project. Different requests are eligible.
- Funding form: Budget-based grant (paid using approved costs or rates for the funded work).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 133–140 · Specific conditions

Innovative technologies and solutions to improve wave and tidal energy systems · Budget overview

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
For-profit organisations can receive up to 70% towards wave and tidal energy systems.
- For-profit organisations: Up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow), leaving at least 30% to cover.
- Non-profit legal entities: Up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow).
- Co-financing conditions: Beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) administering onward grants receive their own funding rate on the eligible amounts paid.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Innovative technologies and solutions to improve wave and tidal energy systems · Topic Q&A 87774

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Separate the core wave and tidal demonstrations from the funding reserved for awards to outside organisations.
- Caps or mandatory allocations: Up to EUR 800,000 cumulatively per third-party recipient. Demonstrations should use at most EUR 24 million of European Union funding, and management should stay at or below 7%.
- Caps or mandatory allocations: Up to EUR 3 million for breakthrough awards and up to EUR 6 million expected for validation awards.
- Eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow): Onward grants are reimbursed to beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) as actual costs.
cards.sources:

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Plan cash flow for wave and tidal energy systems around the initial advance and later payments.
- Payment model: Pre-financing (an advance at the start of the grant) usually precedes periodic payments and the final balance.
- Retention or guarantee: The mutual insurance mechanism (a common fund covering grant recovery risks) deducts 5–8% of the maximum grant from pre-financing.
- Financial reporting or audit: Keep evidence of onward grants charged as actual costs at the beneficiary (organisations formally responsible for funded work)’s reimbursement rate.
cards.sources:

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Apply for wave and tidal energy systems through the European Funding & Tenders Portal in one stage.
- Full proposal: 31 March 2027, 17:00 Brussels time. Submit Part A (online administration form) and Part B (technical proposal) with a 60-page limit.
- Opening: 3 December 2026.

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The Commission estimates around 60 months for the core wave and tidal project.
- Required start: Work normally starts after the grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) is signed. A reasoned exception needs approval.
- Estimated duration: About 60 months for the core action.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
The Commission’s timetable for assessing and contracting wave and tidal energy systems is indicative.
- Expected invitation or assessment result: Around five months from the full-proposal deadline.
- Grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules): Around eight months from the full-proposal deadline.
- Conditions before starting: The beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) must conclude a written consortium agreement (the partners’ written agreement on how the project will run).
cards.sources:

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The wave and tidal proposal must explain how the consortium will run its demonstrations and award grants to outside organisations.
- Application form: Complete online Part A and upload technical Part B and applicable annexes.
- Registration: Beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) and affiliated entities (organisations legally linked to funded partners) need a participant identification code before submission.
- Partner documents: The coordinator confirms its authority to act for the applicant group at submission. Participants sign declarations of honour (signed confirmations of eligibility and other requirements) before grant signature.
- Mandatory annexes and details: Describe the third-party grant calls, advisory-board recruitment and readiness milestones.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Wave and tidal energy systems proposals compete on research quality, impact and the quality of the delivery plan.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence, impact, and quality and efficiency of implementation.
- Thresholds: At least 3/5 on each criterion and 10/15 overall.
- Ranking rules: Ties first favour uncovered topic aspects. The next criteria are impact then excellence.
- Weighting: The impact score (the score for what the project is expected to achieve) has a 1.5 multiplier for ranking.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 28–29 · Evaluation procedure and ranking

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Plan every wave and tidal deployment around an explicit decision with documented engineering, permits and a business plan.
- Conditional — Before each deployment decision: Have the permits, detailed compliant engineering and business and implementation plans in place.
- Recommended: Use relevant European ocean-energy research facilities where they suit the demonstrator.
- Conditional — Satellite data or services: Use Copernicus for Earth observation and/or Galileo or the European Geostationary Navigation Overlay Service for satellite positioning, navigation or timing where the proposal uses the covered services.
- Conditional — Consortium establishment: The destination excludes entities established in China from these Innovation Actions.
